key_insight: Ferroelectricity in Aurivillius CaBi2B2O9 (B = Ta, Nb) is driven by a trilinear coupling of polar and octahedral rotation/tilt modes, with interlayer sliding between Bi2O2 and perovskite blocks as the core structural mechanism.
engineering_relevance: This provides a design rule for layered ferroelectrics: tune stacking-induced interlayer displacement to achieve robust polarization, piezoelectric response, and intrinsic insulation at high temperature.
method: Group-theoretic mode decomposition of the A21am phase
First-principles calculations to evaluate energy landscape and polarization
Analysis of structural distortions and layer-resolved atomic displacements
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic first-principles and symmetry analysis showing that the Γ5−X2+X3− trilinear coupling deepens the ferroelectric well and explains polarization, piezoelectricity, and insulation in both Ta- and Nb-based compounds.
watch_item: The mechanism is inferred from idealized structural/electronic calculations, so experimental validation under realistic defects, strain, and finite-temperature conditions is still needed.
paper_title: The origin of ferroelectricity, polarization and high resistivity in Aurivillius CaBi2B2O9 (B = Ta, Nb)
